issues.legal_issue: A later change to general civil-procedure rules governing writ proceedings does not displace an earlier interpretation of the special territorial-jurisdiction provision when that interpretation did not rely on those general rules.
material_facts: A Division Bench declined to follow the Supreme Court’s earlier interpretation of the special territorial-jurisdiction provision, reasoning that a later explanation to the general civil-procedure law had changed the position for writ proceedings.
The earlier Supreme Court decision had interpreted the special provision without relying on the general civil-procedure law.
issues.conclusion: The later explanation did not affect the earlier interpretation, which remained applicable; the Division Bench’s reasoning for not following it was perverse.
issues.legal_principle: The special territorial-jurisdiction provision must be interpreted according to its own terms. The interpretation in Nasiruddin v. State Transport Appellate Tribunal, AIR 1976 SC 331, did not rely on the Code of Civil Procedure, so the later addition of an Explanation to Section 141 of that Code did not displace it.

predicates.writ_jurisdiction_dispute: The proceeding concerns the territorial jurisdiction of a court to hear a writ petition.
predicates.earlier_interpretation_of_special_territ: A court had previously interpreted a special rule governing territorial jurisdiction.
predicates.earlier_interpretation_did_not_rely_on_g: The earlier court reached its interpretation without relying on general procedural rules.
predicates.later_change_addresses_general_procedure: A later change concerns general procedural rules applicable to proceedings of this kind.

issues.definition: When a writ-jurisdiction dispute concerns a special territorial rule previously interpreted without reliance on general procedure, a later change to general procedure leaves that interpretation applicable.

issues.legal_issue: A designated bench has territorial jurisdiction over a writ petition when the cause of action arises wholly or partly within the area assigned to that bench.
material_facts: A writ petition challenged a government notification and advertisement concerning the proposed sale of six sugar factories, five of which were outside the Oudh area and one within it.
The notification and advertisement were issued by the government at Lucknow, and the grievance arose from that government action.
The question was whether the Lucknow bench or the court sitting at Allahabad could hear the petition.
issues.conclusion: The Lucknow bench had jurisdiction because the cause of action arose at least in part within the Oudh area; where the cause of action is divided between the areas, the litigant may bring the proceeding in either competent forum.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226 of the Constitution and clause 14 of the High Court (Amalgamation) Order, 1948, jurisdiction depends on where the cause of action arose. Nasiruddin v. State Transport Appellate Tribunal, AIR 1976 SC 331, holds that the Lucknow bench has jurisdiction if the cause of action arises wholly or partly in the specified Oudh areas; when it arises partly there and partly outside, the litigant may proceed in either forum. The Court also referred to Ram Rakh Vyas v. Union of India, AIR 1977 Rajasthan 243, in considering the meaning of the relevant expression.

predicates.writ_proceeding: A litigant has brought a writ petition challenging government action or another alleged legal wrong.
predicates.cause_of_action_wholly_or_partly_in_desi: The facts giving rise to the writ petition occurred wholly or partly within the area assigned to a particular bench.

issues.definition: If a writ petition arises wholly or partly from events within an area assigned to a bench, that bench has territorial jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A judgment of a lower bench that has been overruled by a larger bench no longer remains the law to be followed.
material_facts: A Division Bench decided the interpretation of a territorial-jurisdiction provision.
A Full Bench of the same High Court later held that the Division Bench decision was contrary to the law laid down by the Supreme Court and was not correctly decided.
The High Court Registry was nevertheless being asked to comply with directions in the Division Bench judgment.
issues.conclusion: The overruled judgment was no longer the law of the land and was to be treated as non-est; judicial propriety required the judges concerned to follow the law laid down by the larger bench.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment is the judgment of the court, not of the individual judge. It remains effective until set aside or its correctness is doubted by a higher court; once overruled by a larger bench, it no longer remains law and is treated as non-est. Judicial propriety requires judges to follow the governing law rather than persist in directions based on an overruled decision.

predicates.intra_court_precedent_conflict: Different benches of the same court have addressed the same legal issue.
predicates.smaller_bench_judgment_overruled_by_larg: A larger bench has held that the smaller bench’s judgment was not correctly decided.

issues.definition: When a larger bench overrules a smaller bench’s judgment on the same issue, the overruled judgment is no longer governing law.

issues.legal_issue: A bench should await the decision of a larger bench when that larger bench is already considering the same question of law.
material_facts: The question of territorial jurisdiction had already been referred to a Full Bench for consideration.
While that question remained pending before the Full Bench, a Division Bench decided the same question in another matter.
issues.conclusion: The appropriate course for the Division Bench was to await the Full Bench’s decision.
issues.legal_principle: Judicial propriety requires a smaller bench to defer deciding a question that is already under consideration by a larger bench of the same court.

predicates.same_question_pending_before_larger_benc: A larger bench is considering a legal question that has been referred to it.
predicates.smaller_bench_considers_same_question: A smaller bench is asked to decide that same legal question while the larger bench’s consideration remains pending.

issues.definition: If a larger bench is already considering a legal question, a smaller bench asked to decide that question should await the larger bench’s decision.
